content.label: Quote request context panel
content.html:
Quote request

The best first message is specific, not technical.

You do not need to know the final rink size before reaching out. Share the event basics and any known venue constraints so the rental fit can be reviewed.

Include these details

  • Event date or date range
  • City, state, venue, and surface type
  • Indoor, outdoor, covered, or exposed setup
  • Expected attendance and operating hours
  • Access, loading, setup, and teardown notes

content.label: Response and privacy expectations
content.html:
What happens after you send the request

The review team should use your details to understand timing, location, venue fit, and the next planning questions. Final response timing, lead routing, and email behavior must be approved before production.

Privacy note: contact details should only be used to respond to the submitted rink rental inquiry and should not expose private routing information in public page code.

content.title: Quote request questions
content.subtitle: These answers keep the form focused and realistic.

items.question: Can I request a quote before every detail is final?
items.answer: Yes. Share the details you have now, especially date, location, venue type, guest count, and surface notes. The scope can be refined during follow-up.

items.question: What information helps most?
items.answer: Date range, operating hours, venue address, indoor or outdoor placement, surface type, access, expected attendance, and add-on needs are the most useful first details.

items.question: Will this form send to a real inbox yet?
items.answer: Not until the production static form endpoint and lead recipient reference are approved. This template intentionally uses non-secret placeholders.

items.question: Can I ask about service in my city?
items.answer: Yes. Include your city and state. Final availability should be confirmed through quote review rather than assumed from a public page.

content.title: Helpful details for a quote
content.subtitle: The more context you can share, the easier it is to understand availability, setup needs, and rental fit.

cards.title: Event date
cards.description: Include your preferred date, backup dates, setup window, operating hours, and teardown expectations.

cards.title: Location
cards.description: Share the venue address, city, access notes, loading area, and whether the event is public or private.

cards.title: Indoor or outdoor
cards.description: Tell us whether the rink would be inside, outside, covered, or exposed to weather.

cards.title: Surface type
cards.description: Describe the surface, available footprint, slope concerns, power access, and nearby constraints.

cards.title: Expected attendance
cards.description: Estimate guest count, participant volume, event flow, age range, and whether skating is the main attraction.

cards.title: Add-ons
cards.description: Mention skate support, attendants, lighting, music, decor, branding, seating, or hospitality needs.

content.title: Quote request questions
content.subtitle: These answers help set expectations before the rental team follows up.

items.question: What should I include in a quote request?
items.answer: Include date, location, indoor or outdoor placement, available space, surface type, guest count, rental duration, and add-ons.

items.question: Can I request pricing before all details are final?
items.answer: Yes. Early details can start the conversation, and the rental scope can be refined as the venue, timing, and event goals become clearer.

items.question: Do you need venue photos or layout details?
items.answer: Photos, site maps, measurements, and access notes are helpful because they clarify footprint, surface, loading, and guest-flow needs.

items.question: What happens after I submit the form?
items.answer: The next step is to review availability, venue fit, setup considerations, add-ons, and any details needed to shape quote options.
